result.topic_en: Calculations on the Landen/Gauss transformation of elliptic integrals and the arithmetic-geometric mean iteration ($m'=\frac{m+n}{2}$, $n'=\sqrt{mn}$) applied to $\int dt/\sqrt{mm\cos t^2+nn\sin t^2}$.
result.transcription:
$\frac{\partial x}{\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-kkx^2)}} = \frac{\partial y}{\sqrt{(1-y^2)\left(\left(\frac{1+k'}{2}\right)^2-\left(\frac{1-k'}{2}\right)^2 yy\right)}}$ \qquad $k'=1-kk$
$\frac{1}{x} = \frac{1+k'}{2}\frac{1}{y} + \frac{1-k'}{2}y$
$\left(\frac{1}{xx}\right) = \left(\frac{1+k'}{2}\right)^2\frac{1}{yy} + \left(\frac{1-k'}{2}\right)^2 yy + \frac{k^2}{2}$ \qquad $x \mid \sin t$
$\left(\frac{1}{xx}-kk\right) = \left(\frac{1+k'}{2}\frac{1}{y} - \frac{1-k'}{2}y\right)^2$ \qquad $y \mid \sin t_{EV}$[?]
$\left(\frac{1}{xx}-1\right) = \left(\frac{1}{yy}-1\right)\left(\left(\frac{1+k'}{2}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{1-k'}{2}\right)^2 yy\right)$

$\frac{\partial t}{\sqrt{\cos t^2 + k'^2\sin t^2}}$ \qquad $k'=\frac{n}{m}$

$J=\int_0^t \frac{\partial t}{\sqrt{mm\cos t^2+nn\sin t^2}} = \int_0^{t'}\frac{\partial t'}{\sqrt{m'm'\cos t'^2+n'n'\sin t'^2}} = \int_0^{t''}\frac{\partial t''}{\sqrt{m''m''\cos t''^2+n''n''\sin t''^2}} = \int_0^{\theta}\frac{\partial\theta}{\sqrt{\mu\mu\cos\theta^2+\mu\mu\sin\theta^2}} = \frac{1}{\mu}\theta$
[-$\Delta t$-] $\Delta'$
$\frac{1}{\sin t} = \frac{m+n}{2m}\frac{1}{\sin t'} + \frac{m-n}{2m}\sin t'$
$m'=\frac{m+n}{2}$ \quad $n'=\sqrt{mn}$
$\cot t = \cot t'$ [-...-] $\frac{\Delta'^2}{m^2}$
$\operatorname{tg} t = \operatorname{tg} t'\frac{m}{\Delta'} = $ [-$\operatorname{tg} t''$-] $\frac{m}{\Delta'}\frac{m'}{\Delta''}\operatorname{tg} t''$
$\sqrt{mm\cos t^2+nn\sin t^2} = \Delta$

$mk'=n$
$m$ \qquad $n$
$m'=\frac{m+n}{2}$ \quad $n'=\sqrt{mn}$
$m''=\frac{m'+n'}{2}$ \quad $n''=\sqrt{m'n'}$
$\Delta = \sqrt{mm\cos t^2+nn\sin t^2}$
$\Delta' = \sqrt{\frac{mm'(\Delta+n)}{\Delta+m}}$

$\frac{1}{x} + \sqrt{\frac{1}{xx}-kk} = (1+k')\frac{1}{y}$
$\frac{1}{x}\sqrt{\frac{1}{xx}-kk} + \frac{k'}{x} = 2\left(\frac{1+k'}{2}\right)^2\frac{1}{y} - \left(\frac{1-k'}{2}\right)^2 y$
[-$\frac{\Delta+m}{\Delta+n}$-] $=$
$\frac{\Delta+n}{\Delta+m} = \frac{\Delta'^2}{m^2}\frac{m}{m'}$
$\Delta' = \sqrt{\frac{mm'(\Delta+n)}{m+\Delta}}$
